conventions.convention: The underlying manifold is smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and boundaryless; the classical action domain permits a time-oriented C3 Lorentzian metric of signature (-,+,+,+) and global C2 real potential and complex scalar fields. Smooth configurations form a subclass.

The global real potential gives F=dA. The coupling λ is arbitrary real; no integer-weight circle representation or nontrivial bundle sector is assumed. Gauge transformations are A↦A+dχ and φ↦exp(iλχ)φ.

Length coordinates use x0=ct. The dimensionless scalar has charged derivative P_a=∂_aφ−iλA_aφ; A_a has units Wb/m, λ has units Wb⁻¹, Kφ>0 has units J/m, V has units m⁻², and χ has units Wb. The sourced Maxwell sign is ∇_aF^{ab}=−μ0j^b.
Actions are finite global integrals when available and otherwise relative compact actions. Stationarity tests independent smooth compact inverse-metric, real one-form and complex scalar directions.

The evolution theorem assumes Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Its periodic branch requires integer s≥5, h and φ0 in H^{s+1}, the other complete data in H^s, uniformly positive h, the specified compact admissible state range, and all displayed constraints and compatibility conditions. Geometric uniqueness up to isometry and a single smooth real gauge function is asserted for the smooth branch.

The spatial charged compatibility is π_i=∂_iφ0−iλAΣ,iφ0. The spatial Levi-Civita derivative is a distinct operator. The second fundamental form is K(X,Y)=g(∇_Xn,Y), fixing the displayed Einstein constraint signs.
The zero-scalar sector assumes V(0)=0 and zero scalar Cauchy data; it does not require V′(0)=0. All conclusions are conditional model deductions without empirical premises.

alerts.finding: Proof step 2.1 says that multiplying the ith compatibility equation by g^{ki} gives spatial coefficient “−g^{ki}∂_kπ_0”. The compatibility equation contains ∂_iπ_0, so the multiplied expression is −g^{ki}∂_iπ_0, summed over i with k free. The subsequent displayed principal matrices are correct; this is an index typo in the explanatory proof sentence.
